readerTitle: 5,000 downloads and almost no bookings: growing a cleaning app
caseNote: 가상 사례 (청소 예약 앱, 가족 식당 주문 앱) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 앱을 키우는 일은 다운로드를 늘리는 일이 아니라, 고객이 어디서 빠져나가는지 찾아 한 번에 하나씩 고치고, 만족한 고객이 생긴 뒤에 추천을 붙이는 순서의 문제다.
misconception: 앱이 안 크면 광고나 추천 보상으로 다운로드를 더 늘리면 된다.

sources.text: PIXO 유닛 MKT-05 개념 레슨 (유입·활성화·유지, 추천, 성장 실험)

factChecks.note: 퍼널 계산: 다운로드 5,000 → 가입 2,000(40%) → 첫 예약 400(가입자의 20%) → 60일 내 재예약 240(첫 예약자의 60%). 가입에서 첫 예약 단계에서 1,600명(80%)이 빠짐.
실험 계산: 신규 가입 600명을 300명씩 나눔. 기존 화면 20% = 60건, 즉시 가격 화면 30% = 90건. 모두 설명용 가상 수치.

cards.title: 5,000 downloads and almost no bookings
body: Maya runs a home cleaning company with 12 cleaners. She built a booking app and spent $4,000 on ads.
The app was downloaded 5,000 times. Her calendar barely changed. Where did all those people go?

image.label: Phone showing many downloads beside a nearly empty booking calendar
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 왼쪽에 다운로드 숫자가 크게 뜬 스마트폰, 오른쪽에 거의 빈 주간 청소 예약 달력. 청소 도구(대걸레, 스프레이)가 옆에 놓임. 실제 앱 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Where should next month's effort go?
body: Maya has one month and a small budget. Which move comes first?

options.text: Double the ads to get 10,000 downloads
options.feedback: More **acquisition** brings more people, but if most leave before booking, you pay twice as much to fill the same leaky bucket.

options.text: Find the step where people drop out before their first booking
options.feedback: This reads the path as **acquisition, activation, retention**. Fixing the biggest leak makes every future download worth more.

options.text: Add a referral bonus so current users bring friends
options.feedback: Referrals can work, but friends would hit the same leak. It's cheaper to fix it first, then invite.

cards.title: Follow 5,000 downloads.
body: The biggest drop is between signing up and booking. **Four out of five** people who made an account never booked a clean.

cards.title: The leak is activation, not acquisition.
body: **Activation** is the first moment a customer gets real value. For Maya, that's a clean on the calendar.
Her app asked new users for photos of every room, then made them wait 24 hours for a quote. Most closed the app and forgot.
The good news sits lower down: 60% of first-timers book again. People who try the service like it. They just struggle to get there.

cards.title: How should Maya test a fix?
body: Her idea: show an instant flat price for standard apartments, with no photos and no wait.

options.text: Launch it with a new design, lower prices and a discount, all at once
options.feedback: Bookings may rise, but she won't know which change caused it. A **growth experiment** changes one thing so the result teaches something.

options.text: Show instant pricing to half of new sign-ups for two weeks and compare first bookings
options.feedback: A clean **growth experiment**: one change, a comparison group, one number to watch.

options.text: Survey users on whether they'd like instant pricing
options.feedback: Cheap and quick, but people's answers often differ from what they do. A live test measures real bookings.

cards.title: From 60 bookings to 90.
body: Over two weeks, 600 people signed up. The 300 who saw the old screen made 60 first bookings (20%). The 300 who saw instant pricing made 90 (30%).
Now each ad dollar brings in more booked cleans. And with more happy repeat customers, Maya finally has people worth asking for **referrals**.

image.label: Two bars: 60 bookings versus 90 bookings
image.brief: 막대 두 개 비교. 왼쪽 "Old screen: 60", 오른쪽 "Instant price: 90". 오른쪽 막대를 강조색으로. 각 막대 아래 "300 sign-ups" 표기.

cards.title: Growth can outrun the business behind the app.
body: Maya has 12 cleaners. If bookings jump faster than she can hire, cleans get rushed or cancelled, and that 60% return rate falls.
Small tests can also mislead. A two-week result with a few hundred people is a strong hint, not proof. Run it again before betting the budget on it.

cards.title: Now it's a family restaurant's ordering app.
body: Regulars love the app and order often. The owner wants a referral program. Which design fits best?

options.text: $15 credit for every friend who downloads the app
options.feedback: It pays for downloads, not orders. People can game it, and many new users never order.

options.text: After a customer's third order, offer both them and a friend a free dessert on the friend's first order
options.feedback: **Referrals** work best when you ask happy customers and reward a real first order. A dessert also costs less than cash and shows off the food.

options.text: A permanent 10% discount for anyone who shares a link
options.feedback: Sharing may rise, but the discount cuts into every future order, even from people who would have shared anyway.

cards.title: Fix the leak, test one change, then invite friends.
body: Concepts used: **acquisition, activation, retention** to find where people drop out, **growth experiments** to test a fix, and **referrals** once customers are happy.
**Try it today:** count how many new customers reach their first real use of your product. Find the one step where most of them stop.
